mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.0% indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS <= 2.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market that increases inflation expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.8% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth exceeds 0.5% in the past three months, it indicates a tight labor market that may trigger inflationary pressures and central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.
